title: Azure Files and Blob Storage

header.html: Create and configure a file share in Azure Storage; create and configure a container in Blob Storage; configure storage tiers; configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files; configure blob lifecycle management; configure blob versioning
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

toc.title: Lifecycle management, versioning and soft delete

html:
1Azure Files

Azure Files gives fully managed file shares in the cloud, reachable over SMB (and NFS on Premium) and mountable from Windows, Linux and macOS.

Topic Fact
Create Create a file share in a storage account, set a quota and a tier
Mount Use the mount script from the portal (SMB uses port 445, which some networks block)
Tiers Transaction optimized, Hot, Cool (standard accounts); Premium (SSD)
Snapshots Share snapshots are point-in-time, read-only copies; incremental (only changes use space)
Soft delete Keeps a deleted share for a retention period (1 to 365 days) so it can be undeleted

Exam tip

. "Recover a share that was deleted by mistake" = soft delete for Azure Files. "Recover an older version of files in a share" = share snapshots.

2Blob Storage

Blob Storage holds unstructured objects in containers.

Blob type Use
Block blob Documents, images, media (most common)
Append blob Logs (append only)
Page blob Random access, VM disks
Container setting Meaning
Public access level Private (default), Blob (anonymous read of blobs), Container (anonymous list and read)
Access control RBAC, SAS, stored access policy, access keys

3Access tiers

Tier For Storage cost Access cost
Hot Frequently accessed data Highest Lowest
Cool Infrequent, kept at least 30 days Lower Higher
Cold Rare, kept at least 90 days Lower still Higher
Archive Rarely accessed, kept at least 180 days, offline Lowest Highest, must be rehydrated (hours) before reading

Minimum retention periods apply (early deletion charges). [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Archive blobs cannot be read until rehydrated to hot or cool.

4Lifecycle management, versioning and soft delete

Feature What it does
Lifecycle management Rules that move blobs to cooler tiers or delete them based on age (since modification or creation) or last access
Versioning Automatically keeps previous versions when a blob is overwritten or deleted; you can restore an older version
Soft delete (blobs, containers) Retains deleted blobs or containers for a set period for recovery
Snapshots (blobs) Manual point-in-time read-only copy
Exam tip

. "Move blobs to cool after 30 days and delete after one year" = a lifecycle management rule.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Users need a shared network drive in Azure that Windows and Linux machines can mount. Which service fits?

  • ABlob storage
  • BTable storage
  • CQueue storage
  • DAzure Files
Show the answer

Answer: D. Azure Files provides SMB and NFS file shares.

S2A file share was deleted by mistake. What should have been enabled?

  • AA resource lock only
  • BSoft delete for Azure Files
  • CA SAS token
  • DArchive tier
Show the answer

Answer: B. Soft delete retains deleted shares for recovery.

S3Data is rarely accessed and can wait hours to be read. Which tier is cheapest to store?

  • AHot
  • BCool
  • CArchive
  • DPremium
Show the answer

Answer: C. Archive has the lowest storage cost and requires rehydration.

S4Blobs should move to the cool tier after 30 days automatically. What should be configured?

  • AA budget
  • BObject replication
  • CA lifecycle management rule
  • DA lock
Show the answer

Answer: C. Lifecycle rules transition blobs based on age.

S5A blob is overwritten and the old content must be recoverable. What should be enabled?

  • AA firewall
  • BBlob versioning
  • CTags
  • DA static website
Show the answer

Answer: B. Versioning keeps previous versions of blobs.

S6A container allows anonymous read access to individual blobs but not listing. Which public access level is this?

  • ABlob
  • BContainer
  • CPrivate
  • DArchive
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Blob level allows anonymous reads of blobs but not listing the container.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which protocols does Azure Files support?

Show the answer

SMB (and NFS on Premium).

R2What is a share snapshot?

Show the answer

A point-in-time, read-only copy of a file share.

R3Name the four blob tiers.

Show the answer

Hot, cool, cold and archive.

R4What must happen before an archive blob can be read?

Show the answer

It must be rehydrated to hot or cool.

R5What does lifecycle management do?

Show the answer

Moves blobs to other tiers or deletes them by rules.

R6Which blob type suits logs?

Show the answer

Append blob.
